must_find.summary: The subscriptions table has no UNIQUE (account_id, plan_id) constraint (D1). Duplicate subscriptions are possible, and subscribe's INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (account_id, plan_id) will fail at runtime in Postgres because no matching unique constraint exists.
status is declared `text DEFAULT 'active'`: nullable and with no CHECK limiting it to trialing/active/past_due/canceled (D2).
The index is on (status) alone instead of (account_id, status) as D3 requires, so the per-account active lookup isn't served (the plan explicitly rejected a status-only index).

nice_to_find.summary: Explicitly notes that ON CONFLICT (account_id, plan_id) errors without the unique constraint, so subscribe is broken, not merely unprotected.
Tests use a fake connection that only checks SQL text, so they can't catch the missing constraint.

must_not_flag.summary: decoy: the index name ix_subscriptions_status differs from the plan's suggested name; the plan marks names as suggestions. Flagged only if the NAME itself is presented as a problem (the wrong columns are the real issue).
decoy: column order in CREATE TABLE differs from the plan's listing (plan_id before account_id, status last).
decoy: migration file names (003_subscriptions.sql, 004_subscriptions_status_index.sql) differ from the plan's suggested names.
decoy: the index migration correctly uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY with the -- migrate: no-transaction marker; that part conforms.
